title: Magneto-transport and electronic structure studies of ternary antimonides, La$T$Sb$_2$ ($T$ = Cu, Ag)
authors: Himanshu Pant, Neeraj Bhatt, Deepali Sharma, Asif Ali, A. Thamizhavel, Saurabh Singh, Kentaro Kuga, Tsunehiro Takeuchi, Ravi Shankar Singh, R. Bindu
abstract: We investigate Sb square net-based Dirac semimetallic ternary antimonides La$T$Sb$_2$ ($T$ = Cu, Ag) using magnetotransport and photoelectron spectroscopic studies, complemented by density functional theory (DFT) based ab initio calculations. Our results show that both compounds exhibit a positive temperature coefficient of resistivity, linear magnetoresistance (MR), and a deviation from Fermi liquid behaviour at low temperatures (2-30 K). But only $T$ = Ag compound exhibit signature of charge density wave (CDW) phenomena and the results of its temperature dependent MR data suggest that single-band semiclassical transport is not sufficient to understand the transport behaviour. $\text{DFT}+U$ studies show that in both samples, an on-site Coulomb interaction ($U$) for Cu 3$d$ and Ag 4$d$ electrons, in the presence of spin-orbit coupling (SOC) is required to reproduce experimental valence band spectra. Sb 3$d$, 4$d$ core-level spectra combined with $\text{DFT}+U$ calculations and La 3$d$ spectra confirm the presence and effects of inequivalent Sb sites for both the samples. In contrast to the $T$ = Cu compound, which follows expected temperature-dependent core-level sharpening, the $T$ = Ag compound exhibits an anomalous low-temperature broadening in the CDW phase. The analysis of Sb 3$d$ spectra suggests Sb square nets are linked to CDW phenomena in the $T$ = Ag compound. Temperature-dependent ultraviolet photoemission spectroscopic studies on $T$ = Ag show a small decrement in spectral DOS at the $ε_F$ for the temperature below the CDW transition temperature. These core-level studies provide a valuable spectroscopic benchmark for comparing CDW and non-CDW systems and clarifying the role of local electronic environments in CDW formation.
summary: This work characterizes the electronic structure and transport properties of $	ext{LaT}	ext{Sb}_2$ ($	ext{T} = 	ext{Cu}, 	ext{Ag}$) using magnetotransport and photoelectron spectroscopy. The findings reveal that the $	ext{Ag}$ compound exhibits CDW behavior, which is spectroscopically linked to the $	ext{Sb}$ square nets. The study underscores the necessity of correlated electron treatments ($	ext{DFT}+U$) to accurately model the electronic states in these complex materials.
main_problem: The study investigates the electronic structure and transport properties of ternary antimonides, LaTSb2, focusing on the interplay between Charge Density Wave (CDW) order and other emergent phenomena.
main_result: The Ag-containing compound exhibits clear signatures of CDW phenomena, which are linked to the Sb square nets, while both compounds show deviations from Fermi liquid behavior and require advanced theoretical treatments to explain their electronic spectra.
method: The research combines magnetotransport measurements, temperature-dependent photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS/UPS), and ab initio Density Functional Theory calculations, specifically utilizing the DFT+U method.
model_or_system: The physical system is the ternary antimonide $	ext{LaT}	ext{Sb}_2$ ($	ext{T} = 	ext{Cu}, 	ext{Ag}$), which crystallizes in a tetragonal structure featuring $	ext{Sb}$ square nets. The analysis probes the electronic behavior across different temperatures and magnetic fields.
key_observables: Resistivity ($ho$), Magnetoresistance ($	ext{MR}$), core-level peak widths (FWHM), Spectral Density of States ($	ext{DOS}$) at the Fermi level ($\epsilon_F$).
important_parameters: Low temperatures (2-30 K), CDW transition temperature ($	ext{T}_{	ext{CDW}}$), and the on-site Coulomb interaction parameter ($U$).
main_assumptions: Single-band semiclassical transport is insufficient to explain the transport behavior in the $	ext{T} = 	ext{Ag}$ compound.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the crystal structure, temperature dependence of resistivity and MR for both compounds, and detailed XPS/UPS spectra comparing high and low temperatures.
paper_structure: The paper systematically presents transport measurements (resistivity and MR) to identify CDW signatures, followed by detailed spectroscopic analysis (core-level and UPS) to probe the local electronic environment and confirm the role of the $	ext{Sb}$ nets in the CDW formation.
why_interesting: The investigation into CDW formation and the necessity of correlated electron models ($	ext{DFT}+U$) to explain spectral features is highly relevant to understanding strongly correlated materials, which is a key area for theoretical condensed matter physicists.
